title: Cotangent complexes and deformations in ringed topoi
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The homotopical algebra in a ringed topos and the cohomology of diagrams on which the cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi and its deformation theory rest. Homotopy sheaves of simplicial sheaves and the free abelian Whitehead theorem, with and without enough points; derived functors of non-additive functors of complexes in a ringed topos (cross-effects and degree, the Dold-Puppe bound, Deligne's homotopy invariance, the Deligne-Lazard theorem, a uniform bound for the derived functor); Koszul complexes and the shift formulas for symmetric, exterior and divided powers, with their products; décalage of simplicial objects, nerves of internal categories, groupoids and monoid actions, and Quillen's comparison of the homotopy theories of categories and simplicial sets; strict simplicial objects, the homology of the categories of simplices of strict simplicial sets, and Deligne's theorem that the categories of large finite ordinals and injective maps are contractible; derived colimits over a small category and over the category of finite ordinals and injective maps; fibred topoi, their total topoi, morphisms, direct images, and modules on total topoi; the cohomology of total topoi: standard resolutions, the cosimplicial complex computing derived direct images and derived limits, and direct images over a fixed index category; simplicial topoi, the décalage of a simplicial topos, the formula Rp_*p^*E = RHom(Z(X), E) for a simplicial object X of a topos, and cohomological descent for hypercoverings; the cohomology of the second total topos through the simplicial topos of a fibred topos, local systems, and a base change criterion; the left adjoints u_! of inverse images of modules on total topoi, their left derived functors and the adjunction RHom(Lu_!E, F) = RHom(E, u^*F), with derived colimits as a special case; local inductive limits as left adjoints, the left adjoints on the second total topos and their derived functors, derived colimits of simplicial modules, and the décalage statements for left adjoints; a duality formula for diagrams in a topos, which computes the Ext groups of a module of the first total topos into a module pulled back from the topos by the cohomology of the second total topos; equivariant sheaves on simplicial topoi: pseudo-categories, the category BX of equivariant sheaves with its two nerves, and coinduced and induced sheaves; the nerves of coinduced and induced modules as derived direct images and left adjoints along the décalages; the comparison of the cohomology and the derived Hom complexes of equivariant modules with those of the total topoi, with group cohomology as an example; the mixed Hom functor from the second total topos to the first, its compatibility with inverse images and derived left adjoints, and the computation of the Ext groups of equivariant modules by cosimplicial Hom groups, with Ext over a group ring and over a quiver as examples; multisimplicial objects and spectral diagrams, spectra of commutative group objects and the derived categories of spectral diagrams; the suspension theorem of Dold and Puppe and the stabilization of non-additive functors; stable derived functors as exact functors, with the free abelian group functor, whose stable homology is the module in degree 0 and vanishes in degree 1, and the symmetric, exterior and divided powers as examples. Simplicial rings and modules in a topos: homotopies, fibrations, cones and paths, and the calculus of fractions for quasi-isomorphisms; the suspension and loop functors, Ext groups, distinguished triangles and their long exact sequences, and the first Ext group described by extensions. Derived tensor products of simplicial modules and of simplicial algebras, and the derived extension of scalars, under which a quasi-isomorphism of simplicial rings induces an equivalence of derived categories. Spectral sequences for the homology of derived tensor products: from Tor groups degree by degree, the Künneth spectral sequence over the homology ring, and the Postnikov spectral sequence. Differential graded modules over a differential graded ring of a topos: truncations, bounded derived categories and truncated rings for rings in nonpositive degrees, derived Hom, derived tensor products and extension of scalars with their bounds, and the comparison of the derived tensor products of simplicial modules with those of their normalized complexes.
prerequisites: sites, sheaves, topoi and sheaves of modules (the Stacks project, chapters Sites and Sheaves and Modules on Sites)
derived categories and derived functors (the Stacks project, chapter Derived Categories)
simplicial objects, the Dold-Kan correspondence and simplicial homotopies (the Stacks project, chapter Simplicial Methods)

simplicial sets, nerves and Kan complexes; test categories and Quillen's Theorem A (programme course Algebraic spaces and stacks, lessons Simplicial sets, nerves and Kan complexes and Test categories and Grothendieck's homotopy programme)

checks.reading: The choice of topics follows Illusie's work on the cotangent complex, which each lesson credits by name. The proofs were written for this course from the Stacks project (sites, modules, derived categories, simplicial methods), the programme's lessons on simplicial sets and test categories, and the free sources listed below. Several statements are proved by routes different from the classical ones: Deligne's contractibility theorem through a contraction of comma categories and Quillen's Theorem A, the homology of categories of simplices through a double complex, and the total topoi through explicit sites.

open_obligations: The Artin-Mazur criterion, which detects weak equivalences of simplicial sets and of categories through cohomology with local coefficients, is not proved; no lesson uses it.

For a good fibred topos whose left adjoints f_! do not preserve fibre products, the second total category is a topos by Giraud's theorem, which is not proved; the lessons use that category as a topos only under the hypothesis of Theorem 4.3 of the lesson on fibred topoi.

The canonical homotopy equivalence between a simplicial object of an additive category with coproducts and its simplicial replacement, its comparison with diagonals of multisimplicial objects, and the corresponding statement for functors on the truncated categories of injective ordinals, are not yet proved; for simplicial modules over a ring of a topos, a quasi-isomorphism between the two is proved (lesson on derived left adjoints on the second total topos, Lemma 4.1).
The comparison of the derived colimit over finite ordinals and injective maps with the termwise colimit is proved when the terms are colimit-acyclic; the general case is not settled.

For simplicial modules, the diagonal of the total décalage is expected to be quasi-isomorphic to the original object; this is not yet proved. Example 1.4 of the lesson on décalage shows that it is not a homotopy equivalence in general.

Diagrams of diagrams and their types are not treated. The adjunction of derived colimits is proved as an isomorphism of RHom complexes for diagrams of modules over a ring of a topos (lesson on left derived functors of left adjoints, Proposition 4.1); for diagrams in a general abelian category it is proved in its Ext form only.
The free abelian Whitehead theorem without hypotheses on points or additivity depends on Barr's theorem on Boolean localizations, which is not proved.
The compatibility of the standard resolutions of total topoi with morphisms of fibred topoi is not treated; the left derived functors of the left adjoints u_! of inverse images of modules need it.
The cohomology of the second total topos is treated when that category is a topos; for an arbitrary good fibred topos this depends on Giraud's theorem (see above).

The base change criterion for direct images on the second total topoi is proved under an additional condition (inverse images on the target carry injectives to totally acyclic sheaves, or finitely many strings of each length start at each object); the general case is not proved.
The formula for Lu_! by standard resolutions of non-flat complexes is proved when the module inverse images of the source are exact as well; without that condition it is not proved.

The left derived functors of the left adjoints u_! on the second total topoi are proved under a condition on the left adjoints f_! of the source (they preserve flat modules and short exact sequences of flat modules); without it they are not proved.

The category BX of equivariant sheaves on a pseudo-category is a topos by Giraud's theorem, which is not proved; the lessons use only that its modules form an abelian category with enough injectives, which is proved directly.

The identification of the nerves of induced modules with left adjoints along the décalage is proved for two-sided pseudo-categories, which include the nerves of internal categories; for other good pseudo-categories it is not proved.

The comparison of all derived Hom complexes of equivariant modules with those of the total topoi is proved under the exactness condition on left adjoints as well as the injectivity condition, and for the first total topos for two-sided pseudo-categories; under the injectivity condition alone it is proved for complexes of modules with invertible structure, which include the structure ring, so for the cohomology.

The compatibility of the mixed Hom functor with inverse images is proved for bounded above complexes, and its compatibility with derived left adjoints for bounded above complexes; the unbounded versions (along a morphism of finite Tor dimension, respectively under exactness of the left adjoints on all complexes) are not proved.
The internal mixed Hom and the duality formula are proved for diagrams in a topos; their versions for diagrams of diagrams are not treated.

The stable homology of the free abelian group functor is computed in degrees 0 and 1 (X and 0). Cartan's values in degrees 2 and 3 (X/2X and the 2-torsion of X) and the vanishing of the rational stable homology in positive degrees are stated with their source and not proved. The identification of this stabilization with Breen's stable Eilenberg-MacLane complex is not treated.

The isomorphisms between the stable derived functors of S^n, Lambda^n and Gamma^n are proved, naturally, for complexes concentrated in nonpositive degrees. Their naturality on all bounded above complexes needs a comparison with the shift isomorphism of the stabilization, which is not carried out.

That the functor from true triangles, short exact sequences of simplicial modules up to quasi-isomorphism, to distinguished triangles is in general not an equivalence is stated without proof; its essential surjectivity and conservativity are proved.

The Künneth spectral sequence for derived tensor products of simplicial modules is constructed as a spectral sequence of abelian sheaves whose first two pages are modules over the homology ring of the simplicial ring; that its higher differentials and the identification of its abutment are linear over the whole homology ring is stated and not proved.

The homomorphism from the Ext groups of the abelian category of simplicial modules to the Ext groups defined through the suspension, obtained from the diagonal of bisimplicial modules, is not treated; nor is the derived extension of scalars on true triangles.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
